summary: Sat out consecutive padded camp practices with a shoulder injury; head coach Dan Campbell downplayed it ("he's good to go") and the team was simply being cautious with a key piece coming off back-to-back 1,000-yard seasons.

Dealing with a groin/psoas injury since leaving an Aug. 11 joint practice with the Cowboys early; still not back in full team drills as of late August, though doing side work and trending toward a return. Week 1 availability is in real question for the Rams' clear WR1.

Traded from Pittsburgh to Dallas this offseason. His 2025 per-game rate reflects a Steelers offense/QB, not the Cowboys' — CeeDee Lamb has publicly said he wants Pickens to thrive alongside him rather than compete for the top target role, and the two have built visible on-field chemistry through camp.

Traded from Miami to Denver (Broncos sent a 2026 1st, 3rd and 4th for Waddle plus a 4th back) this offseason. His 2025 per-game rate reflects Miami's offense entirely; he now joins Bo Nix and a receiving corps that already included Courtland Sutton and Troy Franklin.

Was Denver's clear No. 2 target last season (104 targets, 709 yards, 6 TDs, second only to Sutton). The Broncos' trade for Jaylen Waddle directly compresses his target share — beat reporters explicitly frame him as the player "most affected" by the move.

Remains Denver's established WR1 target-wise entering 2026, but now shares the room with a recently-traded-for Jaylen Waddle — a real change to the target pool his 2025 per-game rate was built on, even though he wasn't the receiver most affected.

Traded from Chicago to Buffalo this offseason and immediately projects as Josh Allen's top perimeter target — the Bills' best WR addition since Stefon Diggs left. His 2025 per-game rate is entirely a Bears-context number under a different QB.

Was evaluated by athletic trainers during a preseason game and sat out subsequent team drills, though he returned to practice participation shortly after. Worth confirming health closer to Week 1 given the short absence.

Missed practice in a walking boot on his right foot during camp — his second season was already inconsistent, and this camp absence adds uncertainty to a make-or-break third year behind newly-acquired DJ Moore and Khalil Shakir.

Signed a contract extension with New Orleans during camp, a signal of a secure long-term WR1 role there. Also had an injury scare during a Day 15 practice; no serious diagnosis has been reported, but it's worth confirming closer to Week 1.

Saints' first-round rookie WR, drawing early praise for his connection with QB Tyler Shough in camp, but has been out of recent practices with a hamstring injury. As a rookie with no NFL stat history, his 2026 role hinges entirely on health and camp usage, not a projectable baseline.

In a genuine three-way target competition with Jakobi Meyers and Parker Washington under new OC Liam Coen, who frequently uses 12 personnel — Meyers and Washington have actually been getting more camp snaps than Thomas so far, even though Thomas has looked sharp with Trevor Lawrence. 2025 target shares (Washington ~1,000 yards, Thomas 728, Meyers 495 in 10 post-trade games) may not hold in 2026's new scheme.
Missed a practice with a quad contusion but returned quickly and has otherwise had a strong camp building on last season's role as Lamar Jackson's top target. Minor, already resolving.

Entering 2026 with QB continuity for the first time in his career — he played with nine different starting QBs across his first four seasons, and is now building chemistry with an established Geno Smith as WR1. A real change to the target-distribution volatility his prior per-game rates were produced under.

Jets' first-round rookie WR (30th overall); slow start to camp drew some concern but has finished camp strong and is being deployed as clear WR3 behind Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell, having pulled ahead of a position battle with Isaiah Williams. No NFL track record to project from yet.

Missed most of camp from early August with a hamstring injury, alongside rookie Makai Lemon; both were full practice participants again by Day 15 (Aug. 24). Not considered serious, but worth confirming health into Week 1.

Eagles' first-round rookie WR (20th overall, 2025 Biletnikoff winner at USC); missed most of camp with a hamstring injury alongside DeVonta Smith, both back to full practice by Aug. 24. As a rookie with zero NFL games, his 2026 role is entirely camp-usage-dependent, not stat-projectable.
Undisclosed injury has kept him out of practice since Aug. 8, though the team and reporters describe it as minor with no Week 1 availability concern as of Aug. 24.

Departed Indianapolis for Pittsburgh this offseason, pairing with DK Metcalf as Aaron Rodgers' top targets. His 2025 per-game rate is a Colts-context number under a different QB and offense. Also nursing a right ankle injury since Aug. 8, described as minor with no Week 1 concern.

Left Tampa Bay (his only team for 12 seasons) to sign a 3-year, $42.4M deal with San Francisco in March 2026, joining a receiving corps now also missing Ricky Pearsall to a season-ending injury. At 33 and coming off an injury-marred 2025, he's also dealing with a new ankle/foot issue in camp — real durability risk alongside the role change.
Continuing to manage a lingering 2024 ankle injury with periodic veteran maintenance days through camp, aiming to open the season fully healthy rather than ramping up camp reps at full volume.
Mike Evans' departure to San Francisco opens real target share in Tampa Bay's passing offense for Godwin and Jalen McMillan to absorb in 2026.

Missed most of 2025 with a severe neck injury; in 2026 camp he's dealt with a knee bang (compression sleeve, described as minor) that cost him a practice. Positioned for a bigger role now that Mike Evans has left for San Francisco, but has almost no healthy-season track record to project a 2026 baseline from.

Signed a 4-year, $141M extension this offseason, cementing his WR1 role; had a minor undisclosed injury held out as precaution in camp but was back to practicing by the time camp opened in full. Atlanta's QB situation (Michael Penix Jr. vs. Tua Tagovailoa, both banged up) is a bigger variable for his 2026 target quality than his own health.

With Michael Pittman traded to Pittsburgh and Alec Pierce still working back from ankle surgery, the Colts have explicitly expanded Downs beyond his prior slot-only role — a real change from the target profile his 2025 per-game rate reflects. Missed a couple of camp practices with a calf issue, described as minor.

Making a real case to be Arizona's most reliable receiver over Marvin Harrison Jr., who has been dealing with drops and uneven route execution through camp. Coach LaFleur has publicly framed the room as Harrison being the Cardinals' Davante Adams to Wilson's Puka Nacua — both project real roles, but Wilson's stock is trending up relative to last season's pecking order.
Missed a week of camp with a sprained right shoulder before returning to practice; entering year 3 with continued questions about durability, though there's no reported Week 1 concern.

Chargers hired Mike McDaniel as offensive coordinator for 2026, a scheme change from the offense that produced McConkey's team-leading 789-yard, 6-TD 2025 season. Camp reports have him bouncing back and remaining the clear starter opposite Quentin Johnston.
Coming off a career-best 2025 (735 yards, 8 TDs on 51 catches), now playing under new OC Mike McDaniel's scheme rather than the one that produced those numbers.

Signed with New England in free agency this offseason, joining a WR room fully re-tooled around a traded-for A.J. Brown. Projects as the Patriots' high-volume slot receiver, a similar role to what departed WR Stefon Diggs held there in 2025 — his own 2025 per-game rate is entirely a different-team number.

Signed with the Washington Commanders this offseason after leading New England in receiving in 2025 — his 2025 per-game rate is a Patriots number under a different QB/scheme entirely. Note: nfl_players roster data may still show his prior team; Washington is his current team as of August 2026.

Was limited by a foot injury for most of his 2025 sophomore season; entering 2026 healthy and drawing praise as a bigger part of Chicago's passing offense (now without DJ Moore, traded to Buffalo) alongside Luther Burden III.

Drew heavy praise through the offseason program and early camp ("most targeted receiver on the field" on Day 2) as Chicago's WR2 behind Odunze in a passing game now without DJ Moore. Has also been dealing with a camp injury ("hobbled" by Day 9) — worth confirming Week 1 health.
Missed a couple of practices after Family Night with an ankle injury but returned during the preseason — a different, more minor issue than the Jones fracture that disrupted his 2025 camp.
Sat out team drills with a thumb injury during camp (still ran routes on air); coach O'Connell confirmed the issue but it hasn't been described as serious.

Minnesota's QB job is contested between Kyler Murray and J.J. McCarthy through camp, with Murray reportedly having the better camp so far — a real change to who's throwing to Jefferson/Addison/Jennings versus 2025, whoever wins the job.
